src/paseo/runtimeInitialTurn.ts strips outputSchema for aeh.kind=semantic-assessment both at materialize and at the continued run; src/paseo/sdk.ts runPaseoSdkAgent then calls handle.run(prompt, {timeoutMs}) only. The installed Paseo stack DOES support provider-enforced JSON output for the initial prompt: @getpaseo/server create.js builds runOptions from create_agent_request.outputSchema and @getpaseo/server opencode-agent.js applies format {type:'json_schema', schema} to session.promptAsync. The installed @getpaseo/protocol@0.9.1 send_agent_message_request carries no outputSchema, so only the creation-time/initial-prompt channel can enforce it.

resolveSemanticAssessor requires selection.runtimeCapabilities.structuredOutput === true for the assessor runtime, and the semantic request requires structuredOutputRequired:true, but the operation-scoped managed path never exercises the provider's structured-output mode; the non-operation path (no aeh.operation label) uses launchManagedPaseoAgent creation with initialPrompt+outputSchema and the round-2 informational lane succeeded through a real mimo session.

The claimed disposition 'real model-output flakiness' cannot be the final classification because the rejected payload was not persisted; the adapter degradation is a verifiable product condition that makes the contract satisfiable only by model prose compliance.
round6RepairContract: Make the operation-scoped semantic assessor turn use provider-enforced structured output: either (a) create the assessor agent with the assessment prompt as initialPrompt plus the semantic-assessment outputSchema so Paseo/OpenCode applies format json_schema, or (b) separate 'provider output schema' from 'AEH structured-result sink activation' in the SDK adapter so a non-participant assessor turn can pass outputSchema without activating the AEH result channel. Preserve: no WorkGraph participant registration, no writer lease, no tools/MCPs, read-only assessor identity, deterministic schema/evidence/binding/provenance validation authoritative.

Keep the deterministic schema unchanged and the total real-model attempts per assessment <= 2 by giving the bounded retry a single owner (collapse the nested STACK correction loop or make its retry count compose to one total) and update the docs claim accordingly.

Persist a bounded, sanitized fingerprint of the rejected raw reply (length + sha256 + first N chars) in the failure details/trace and record failed assessor session ids in lane evidence so the next failure is diagnosable; never coerce or synthesize fields.

Add focused deterministic regressions: the operation-scoped assessor launch carries the provider output schema while NOT activating the AEH result sink; timeout classification and bounded retry unchanged; then one real-provider verification of an operation-scoped STACK/assessment, then rerun change/direct-change to a real terminal ACCEPTED result.

If real verification proves the provider cannot honor json_schema for the selected model, record REAL_PROVIDER_CONTRACT_LIMITATION truthfully with the exact provider error and do not weaken the schema; the full_suite lane must still bind a real successful assessment or a truthful terminal failure.

Root causes are environment/test: the local Paseo daemon reports 'Status details unavailable (DAEMON_REQUEST_TIMEOUT)' persistently, so startPaseoHarness (unmodified src/paseo/start.ts) cannot observe healthy/stopped; and AEH_PASEO_FORCE_CLI=1 blocks the session-scoped assessor SDK launch required since before S13 (runtimeCore guard exists at base). Not an S13 regression.
Both failures are the long-recorded OBJECTIVE_COMPLETION_REQUIRED terminal-fixture failures; reproduced identically at e3dad34 (2/2). Recorded as pre-existing since S6/S7 in the ledger.

Reproduced 3/3 at e3dad34; src/paseo/sdkResolve.ts and the test file are unmodified by S13. The tests expect fixture-local mise stores but the real mise install is resolved; environment drift from the installed Paseo CLI, as recorded at S10/S12.

Current candidate: failed once in the full suite and once in 6 file-isolation runs (1 failure in 19 current executions including the single-test loop); base e3dad34: 0 failures in 19 equivalent executions. Stack proves the test races itself: the descendant writer process is spawned before seed()->saveOperation()->assertWorkspaceMatchesSourceDigest, and saveOperation computes the candidate digest and then asserts it on the same tree while the child writes descendant.pid; in a non-git temp root the inventory is empty ('recent digest inputs: <none>'). The product gate correctly fails closed on a mutated workspace. S13's listWorktreeDigestPaths now issues three git invocations per digest computation instead of one, widening the race window in this non-git fixture. Round 6 must make the fixture deterministic (bind the candidate before spawning the writer or keep the pid file outside the digest root) and may reduce the non-git digest enumeration cost; do not weaken assertWorkspaceSourceDigest.

findings.title: Clean-build asset resolution defect: init resolves templates from stale shared dist/releases assets
findings.detail: packageRoot() in src/core/init.ts resolves `templates/*` as dist/releases/templates, while scripts/build.mjs publishes assets only per release (dist/releases/<id>/templates). The current checkout only works because stale Sep-22 pre-v2 shared copies exist at dist/releases/templates (project.yaml with a quick: block and old agent names, pre-v2 AGENTS.md). A fresh build in a disposable worktree at e3dad34 fails `init` with ENOENT dist/releases/templates/project.yaml (pre-existing, reproduced), and npm pack ships the stale shared copies inside every packed candidate. The S13 packed fixtures were initialized from those stale templates; only the campaign's explicit rewrite of .harness/project.yaml masked it.
findings.requiredRepair: Resolve runtime assets relative to the running release (or publish shared assets at dist/releases atomically) so a clean build + packed init works without stale leftovers; add a regression that a fresh build's init succeeds with no dist/releases/* shared-asset leftovers and that packed init uses the release's own assets. Keep fail-closed behavior.
